Priya R. (Customer Success): FYI raised by customer MediLedger — after SSO provisioning they hit 403 on mixed requests (embeddings + generation). Saying it worked for a week then started failing. ticket: #ML-8421
Jun Park (SRE): Can you paste exact error payload they see? 403 with which code?
Priya R. (Customer Success): From their dev: `{"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"token missing scopes: embeddings,rerank"}`. They only used the key created by our SSO onboarding flow (Okta JIT).
Aisha K. (Support): Repro steps from customer included: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"foo"}'` -> 403. Then tried a text generation call same key -> also 403 on some routes, but some plain metadata calls succeed.
Jun Park (SRE): That error string looks like our backend gating on token scopes (expected). Could be the SSO-scoped service key missing opted-in scopes. Did they use an org-admin or app-only key?
Priya R. (Customer Success): They said the key was created by their IdP admin when they accepted the SSO app consent screen — likely the per-user service key flow.
Luca M. (Platform): Quick checklist: 1) IdP provisioning can request limited scopes via SCIM mapping. 2) Our JIT service currently maps "inference" vs "embeddings"/"rerank" per application claim. If the app claim lacked the embedding flag we generate a key without that scope.
Aisha K. (Support): Is there a quick workaround we can give them? They are blocked in staging.
Luca M. (Platform): Short-term: create a new API key from the Redwood Console under an org-admin account (Settings -> API Keys) and ensure boxes for "Embeddings" and "Rerank" are checked. That bypasses the SSO JIT consent mapping. Long-term: we should make the JIT default include inference+embeddings for enterprise orgs unless explicitly restricted.
Priya R. (Customer Success): I told customer that, they asked for a repro script to validate scopes from their side before regenerating. Can we provide a curl that introspects the key?
Jun Park (SRE): Yes — they can hit our token introspect endpoint: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/token/introspect \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -d '{"token":"<their_key>"}'
``` 
Response will include: `{"active":true,"scopes":["inference","embeddings"]}` or missing ones. Share with them, but highlight they must not post keys in public.
Aisha K. (Support): Also note: mixed requests (batching embeddings + generation in same payload) will be rejected if any required scope absent — common pitfall. We should add that to the KB.
Priya R. (Customer Success): Customer did token introspect and confirmed scopes were ["inference"] only. They want to know why Okta-created keys had reduced scopes.
Luca M. (Platform): Likely root cause: the SSO consent app in Okta had a scopes mapping that omitted embeddings/rerank, and the JIT handler respects IdP-provided scope subset. Two fixes: (A) update IdP app to request full scopes; (B) update our JIT to add missing recommended scopes for org-level integrations.
Jun Park (SRE): Short-term mitigation for them: create a new org-level service key (console) and rotate to it. I'll mark this as recommended for now. Also I've issued a short expiry token if they need ephemeral access for testing.
Priya R. (Customer Success): Customer accepted creating a console key but asked for a rollback-safe plan because they use automated CI that pulls creds from vault. They want to avoid manual rotation.
Luca M. (Platform): If they want automated provisioning: we can create a dedicated service principal (org API client) with proper scopes and provide a small script to exchange an app role assertion for that key. But that's product work. For now, manual rotation + update vault entry.
Aisha K. (Support): Logging note — I found similar pattern in 3 other orgs last quarter. Filing a follow-up to product to update SSO onboarding doc and default JIT scopes.
sso-bot: Okta SCIM app "MediLedger" last_sync=2026-02-18T15:22:10Z, changed_scopes=[]
ticket-bot: Created escalation ML-8421-ESCL, priority=high, linked to internal task PLAT-3179
Jun Park (SRE): For eng triage: attach reproduction trace (we have their curl + response headers). Headers show `x-request-id: req_9b3f...` and upstream error `403: insufficient_scope`.
Luca M. (Platform): I'll pick up PLAT-3179. Proposed ACs: 1) Make JIT add recommended scopes for org-level SSO unless admin opts out. 2) Add console KB warning about SSO key scope differences. 3) Add a diagnostic command in Console to re-request full scopes from IdP.
Priya R. (Customer Success): I'll update MediLedger with the console-key workaround, attach the introspect curl, and keep them updated. Also noted for follow-up to offer migration assistance. :thumbsup:
Aisha K. (Support): Adding KB draft in #docs-support after this thread.
Jun Park (SRE): last check — replication steps for internal: use SSO-provisioned key with scopes ["inference"] and run: ```
# expect 403
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/batch -H "Authorization: Bearer $SSO_KEY" -d '{"tasks":[{"type":"embedding","input":"x"},{"type":"generate","prompt":"y"}]}'
```
Jun Park (SRE): If you want me to run this in a sandbox and attach traces, I will.
Priya R. (Customer Success): Please do, attach to ML-8421-ESCL. End state: customer unblocked by console key rotation; product follow-up for JIT default scopes.
